blocks.text: It was the Sunday after Jesus died. Some of the women had come back from the tomb that morning with a strange report, but most of his friends did not believe them. That afternoon, two of his followers set out from Jerusalem to walk home.

verses.text: And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs.

verses.text: And it came to pass, that, while they communed together and reasoned, Jesus himself drew near, and went with them.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: We trusted. We had hoped. Those may be some of the saddest words two people can say together. They had believed he was the one, and now he was dead, and their hope had died with him.

verses.text: Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre;

blocks.text: Then the stranger began to talk. He went back to the beginning, to Moses and the prophets, and showed them how the scriptures had pointed all along to a Messiah who would suffer and then enter his glory.

verses.text: And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.

blocks.text: It had been a long walk, about seven miles. Now, with night falling, they got straight up and went all the way back.

verses.text: And they told what things were done in the way, and how he was known of them in breaking of bread.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: They set out that day walking away from Jerusalem, sad and done. Jesus came alongside them on the road before they even knew it was him. He listened to their broken hopes, opened the scriptures to them, and stayed when they asked him to. Some days we are walking the Emmaus road too. He still draws near, sometimes before we know it is him.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to Luke 24:13-35; the breaking of bread told as the text tells it, with no position on communion; Jesus's teaching summarised from v26-27 without new words put in his mouth.

cultural.note: Grief and lost hope honoured; plain and hopeful; ends on the story's truth.
